A.explanation: Too short for the accelerating train to cover the goods train distance; at $6\text{ s}$ the goods train is at $60\text{ m}$ but the express is only at $9\text{ m}$.

B.explanation: At $10\text{ s}$ the goods train is at $100\text{ m}$ but the express train is only at $25\text{ m}$, so it has not yet caught up.

C.explanation: At $20\text{ s}$ the express velocity equals $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so it just matches the goods speed but its displacement is only $100\text{ m}$ compared with $200\text{ m}$.

D.explanation: At $40\text{ s}$ both displacements equal $400\text{ m}$, so the express train meets and overtakes the goods train.

hints: Notice the word overtake means the two displacements measured from the station at time $t$ must be equal, not the velocities.
Write the goods train displacement with constant $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ as $s = vt$ and the express train displacement from rest with $0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ as $s = \frac{1}{2}at^{2}$.
Set $10t$ equal to $0.25t^{2}$ and solve for the non-zero $t$, ignoring the $t = 0$ start.
walkthrough: Identify the start: at $t = 0$ both trains are at the station, goods speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ constant, express $u = 0$ with $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Goods train displacement is uniform motion: $s_g = vt = 10t$, with $s$ in $\text{m}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$.
Express train displacement is accelerated from rest: $s_e = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2} = 0 + 0.5 \times 0.5 \times t^{2} = 0.25t^{2}$.
For overtaking set displacements equal: $0.25t^{2} = 10t$. Divide by $t$ for $t > 0$ to give $0.25t = 10$.
Solve $t = 10 / 0.25 = 40\text{ s}$, and check $s_g = 400\text{ m}$ and $s_e = 0.25 \times 1600 = 400\text{ m}$. This is option D.
